clip.tooltip: The CLIP model used for encoding the text.

ckpt_name.tooltip: The name of the checkpoint (model) to load.

images.tooltip: The images to create a video from.

audio.tooltip: The audio to add to the video.

bit_depth.tooltip: Auto uses 8-bit for sRGB and 10-bit for HDR. Explicit 8-bit and 10-bit choices are independent of colorspace.

color_space.tooltip: Colorspace of the input images. HDR selects BT.2020/HLG and HDR PQ selects BT.2020/PQ.

codec.tooltip: Optionally encode the video immediately. None keeps the images in tensor form; Auto uses H.264.

iclora_model.tooltip: Direct output from a LoRA Loader for the specific IC-LoRA from which to extract the metadata.

video.tooltip: The video to extract components from.

image.tooltip: Image or video to condition the latent video on. Must be 8*n + 1 frames. If the video is not 8*n + 1 frames, it will be cropped to the nearest 8*n + 1 frames.

frame_idx.tooltip: Frame index to start the conditioning at. For single-frame images or videos with 1-8 frames, any frame_idx value is acceptable. For videos with 9+ frames, frame_idx must be divisible by 8, otherwise it will be rounded down to the nearest multiple of 8. Negative values are counted from the end of the video.

attention_mask.tooltip: Optional pixel-space spatial mask. Controls per-region conditioning influence via self-attention, multiplied by strength.

iclora_parameters.tooltip: Optional IC-LoRA parameters from a Get IC-LoRA Parameters node. Used for adjusting guide processing as required by certain IC-LoRAs (eg. those with a reference_downscale_factor > 1). When chained, each LTXVAddGuide uses only the parameters connected to it.

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model used for decoding the latent.

batch_size.tooltip: The number of latent audio samples in the batch.

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model to get configuration from.

img_compression.tooltip: Amount of compression to apply on image.

stretch.tooltip: Stretch the sigmas to be in the range [terminal, 1].

terminal.tooltip: The terminal value of the sigmas after stretching.

resize_type.tooltip: Select how to resize: by exact dimensions, scale factor, matching another image, etc.

width.tooltip: Target width in pixels. Set to 0 to auto-calculate from height while preserving aspect ratio.

height.tooltip: Target height in pixels. Set to 0 to auto-calculate from width while preserving aspect ratio.

crop.tooltip: How to handle aspect ratio mismatch: 'disabled' stretches to fit, 'center' crops to maintain aspect ratio.

multiplier.tooltip: Scale factor (e.g., 2.0 doubles size, 0.5 halves size).

longer_size.tooltip: The longer edge will be resized to this value. Aspect ratio is preserved.

shorter_size.tooltip: The shorter edge will be resized to this value. Aspect ratio is preserved.

width.tooltip: Target width in pixels. Height auto-adjusts to preserve aspect ratio.

height.tooltip: Target height in pixels. Width auto-adjusts to preserve aspect ratio.

megapixels.tooltip: Target total megapixels (e.g., 1.0 ≈ 1024×1024). Aspect ratio is preserved.

match.tooltip: Resize input to match the dimensions of this reference image or mask.

crop.tooltip: How to handle aspect ratio mismatch: 'disabled' stretches to fit, 'center' crops to maintain aspect ratio.

multiple.tooltip: Resize so width and height are divisible by this number. Useful for latent alignment (e.g., 8 or 64).

scale_method.tooltip: Interpolation algorithm. 'area' is best for downscaling, 'lanczos' for upscaling, 'nearest-exact' for pixel art.

filename_prefix.tooltip: The prefix for the file to save. This may include formatting information such as %date:yyyy-MM-dd% or %Empty Latent Image.width% to include values from nodes.

format.tooltip: The output container. Auto uses MP4 for Auto/H.264 and WebM for AV1. MP4, MKV, and WebM select a specific container.

codec.tooltip: The output video codec. Auto preserves a compatible source stream. H.264 and AV1 re-encoding support SDR, HDR (HLG), and HDR PQ.

encoding.tooltip: Automatic preserves compatible H.264 streams. Re-encode applies custom encoding options.

crf.tooltip: Lower values produce higher quality and larger files.

encoding.tooltip: Automatic preserves compatible AV1 streams. Re-encode applies custom encoding options.

vae.tooltip: The VAE model used for decoding the latent.

temporal_size.tooltip: Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to decode at a time.

temporal_overlap.tooltip: Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to overlap.

duration.tooltip: Duration in seconds, or 0 for unlimited duration

strict_duration.tooltip: If True, when the specified duration is not possible, an error will be raised.

strategy.tooltip: uniform: evenly spaced, head: first N, tail: last N, random: random sorted.

resolution.tooltip:
Resolution the model runs at (longest side, multiple of 14).
Lower = faster / less VRAM.
Higher = more detail.
Output is upsampled back to the original size.

resize_method.tooltip:
upper_bound_resize: scale so the longest side = resolution (caps memory, default).
lower_bound_resize: scale so the shortest side = resolution (preserves more detail on tall/wide images, uses more memory).

mode.tooltip:
mono: single view image (works with any model variant).
multiview: all images processed together for geometric consistency + camera pose (for Small/Base models only).

ref_view_strategy.tooltip:
Which view acts as the geometric anchor.
- saddle_balanced: the view most 'average' across all others (best general choice).
- saddle_sim_range: the view most visually distinct from the others.
- first / middle: fixed positional picks.

pose_method.tooltip:
How the camera field-of-view is estimated (for Small/Base models only).
- cam_dec: learned from image features.
- ray_pose: derived geometrically from the model's 3D ray output.
Affects perspective correctness of the 3D output. Try both if results look distorted.

output_tooltips:
Dictionary of non-normalized tensors.
Always has the keys: depth, image, mode.
Optional keys: sky (for Mono/Metric), confidence (for Small/Base), extrinsics + intrinsics (for multi-view).
DA3Inference.name: DA3Inference
DA3Inference.description: Run Depth Anything 3 on an image. In multi-view mode each image is treated as a separate view of the same scene.

output.tooltip:
- depth: normalised greyscale depth image.
- depth_colored: depth mapped through the Turbo colormap.
- sky_mask: sky probability in [0, 1] (for Mono/Metric models only).
- confidence: normalised depth confidence (for Small/Base models only).

normalization.tooltip:
- v2_style: mean/std normalisation for perceptually balanced results (default).
- min_max: stretches the full depth range to [0, 1] for maximum contrast.
- raw: no scaling,preserves metric units for Metric model.

apply_sky_clip.tooltip: Clip sky-region depth to the 99th percentile of foreground depth before normalisation. Requires a sky key in the da3_geometry input (for Mono/Metric models only).

normalization.tooltip:
- v2_style: mean/std normalisation for perceptually balanced results (default).
- min_max: stretches the full depth range to [0, 1] for maximum contrast.
- raw: no scaling,preserves metric units for Metric model.

apply_sky_clip.tooltip: Clip sky-region depth to the 99th percentile of foreground depth before normalisation. Requires a sky key in the da3_geometry input (for Mono/Metric models only).

colored.tooltip: Apply the Turbo colormap to the sky mask.
Apply the Turbo colormap to the confidence map.

DA3Render.name: DA3Render
DA3Render.description: Render a depth map, confidence map, or sky mask from Depth Anything 3 geometry data.

resolution.tooltip: Reference images are resized to about resolution x resolution pixels, at multiples of 32, preserving aspect ratio. 0 keeps each reference at its own size, rounded to a multiple of 32.

images.tooltip: Reference images, seen by the text encoder and spliced into the sequence as VAE latents.

output_tooltips: Empty latent on the first reference image's size, to match with sampling as any other size shifts the edit.
TextEncodeQwenImage21.name: TextEncodeQwenImage21

model.tooltip: The model used for denoising the input latent.

seed.tooltip: The random seed used for creating the noise.

steps.tooltip: The number of steps used in the denoising process.

cfg.tooltip: The Classifier-Free Guidance scale balances creativity and adherence to the prompt. Higher values result in images more closely matching the prompt however too high values will negatively impact quality.

sampler_name.tooltip: The algorithm used when sampling, this can affect the quality, speed, and style of the generated output.

scheduler.tooltip: The scheduler controls how noise is gradually removed to form the image.

positive.tooltip: The conditioning describing the attributes you want to include in the image.

negative.tooltip: The conditioning describing the attributes you want to exclude from the image.

denoise.tooltip: The amount of denoising applied, lower values will maintain the structure of the initial image allowing for image to image sampling.

KSampler.name: KSampler
KSampler.description: Uses the provided model, positive and negative conditioning to denoise the latent image.

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model to use for encoding.

latent.tooltip: Video or audio latent to freeze. Audio is 4D; video is 5D.

LTXVFreezeLatent.name: LTXVFreezeLatent
LTXVFreezeLatent.description: Set noise_mask to 0 so this latent is kept clean during sampling. Works on video or audio. Typical uses: freeze audio before Concat AV so it only provides cross-attention, or freeze any latent that should not be denoised.

video_start_time.tooltip: Start time in seconds for the video mask.

video_end_time.tooltip: End time in seconds for the video mask.

audio_start_time.tooltip: Start time in seconds for the audio mask.

audio_end_time.tooltip: End time in seconds for the audio mask.

max_length.tooltip: 'truncate': cut latent to end_time length. 'pad': extend latent to end_time. 'partial': mask range within existing latent.

existing_mask_mode.tooltip: How to combine with existing noise masks if present. 'add' will take the max of existing and new mask, 'overwrite' will replace with new mask. 'subtract' will set the masked region to 0 instead of 1, effectively unmasking it.

LTXVAudioVideoMask.name: LTXVAudioVideoMask
LTXVAudioVideoMask.description: Creates noise masks for video and audio latents based on specified time ranges. New content is generated within these masked regions

model.tooltip: The model to apply context windows to during sampling.

context_length.tooltip: The length of the context window in real frames. Must be 8*n + 1.

context_overlap.tooltip: The overlap of the context window in real frames.

context_schedule.tooltip: Step-dependent scheduling algorithm for context windows.

context_stride.tooltip: The stride of the context window; only applicable to uniform schedules.

closed_loop.tooltip: Whether to close the context window loop; only applicable to looped schedules.

fuse_method.tooltip: The method to use to fuse the context windows.

freenoise.tooltip: Whether to apply FreeNoise noise shuffling, improves window blending.

retain_first_frame.tooltip: Retain the first latent frame in every context window (may help retain initial reference).

split_conds_to_windows.tooltip: Whether to split multiple conditionings (created by ConditionCombine) to each window based on region index.

LTXVContextWindows.name: LTXVContextWindows
LTXVContextWindows.description: Set context windows for LTXV-like models.

source.tooltip: Color space of the input pixels.

destination.tooltip: Color space of the output pixels. Set the save node to this same color space. Convert LogC3 or ACEScct to linear ACEScg for ACEScg EXR, or to linear for Rec.709 EXR. Convert to sRGB/HDR/HDR PQ before saving video.

filename_prefix.tooltip: The prefix for the file to save. May include formatting tokens such as %date:yyyy-MM-dd% or %Empty Latent Image.width%.

format.tooltip: The file format in which to save the image.

input_color_space.tooltip:
Colorspace of the input tensor. The EXR is always written as scene-linear in the matching gamut.
sRGB — input is sRGB-encoded Rec.709; the inverse sRGB EOTF is applied.
HDR — input is HLG-encoded Rec.2020 (BT.2100); the inverse HLG OETF is applied to get scene-linear light.
linear — input is already scene-linear (Rec.709 primaries); written through unchanged. Use this for renderer/compositor output.
linear ACEScg — input is already scene-linear ACEScg (AP1 / D60); written through unchanged with ACEScg chromaticities.

bit_depth.tooltip: Auto uses 8-bit YUV420 for sRGB and 10-bit YUV420 for HDR.

input_color_space.tooltip: Colorspace of the input images. HDR selects BT.2020/HLG and HDR PQ selects BT.2020/PQ.

crf.tooltip: Lower values produce higher quality and larger files.

loop_count.tooltip: Number of times to loop the animation. 0 loops forever.
